title: Saccade planning and attention (Moore & Fallah)
summary: Moore & Fallah (2001) asked whether preparing an eye movement directs attention: monkeys detected a brief dimming of a peripheral target among flashing distractors while the frontal eye field was stimulated below the saccade threshold. This is the behavioural task: fixate, watch a target inside or outside a configurable movement field, press a key when it dims (or hold off on catch trials), with the dimming titrated by the paper's simultaneous block staircase for stimulation and control trials. Microstimulation is a timed STIM_TRIGGER event for the lab's stimulator.
references: Moore, T., & Fallah, M. (2001). Control of eye movements and spatial attention. PNAS, 98(3), 1273–1276. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.98.3.1273

deviations.original: Monkey depresses a lever to start the trial and releases it when the target dims (p. 1273)
deviations.here: A key press (`space`) when the target dims; the trial starts on fixation alone. On a monkey rig a lever box must send the key on release
deviations.reason: alhazen reads key presses, not a held lever; holding the lever before and during the trial is not checked

deviations.original: A 100-ms train of biphasic pulses (0.2 ms, 200 Hz) from a Grass S88 with two PSIU-6 isolation units, at ≤ 50% of the movement-threshold current, through Pt/Ir electrodes in the FEF (pp. 1273–1274)
deviations.here: A STIM_TRIGGER event on the display flip one SOA before the (would-be) dimming, mapped to a TTL line in the rig file; the stimulator, train and current are the lab's. The paper's train values are recorded in each session's params
deviations.reason: This software drives no stimulator; the seam is a declared event and a sync line

deviations.original: A separate paradigm each session: suprathreshold stimulation from five fixation positions; the endpoints from the centre define the MF, and the target is placed there (p. 1274)
deviations.here: Not implemented: the lab maps the MF and enters it as field.movement_field_dva
deviations.reason: It needs the stimulator and a site; it is the lab's procedure, not the behavioural task

deviations.here: Any alhazen eye tracker (the example rigs use an EyeLink)
deviations.reason: Hardware; the fixation-window rule is the same

deviations.original: CORTEX on a 60-Hz monitor, 40 × 30 cm at about 57 cm (p. 1273)
deviations.here: PsychoPy on the rig's monitor; every duration in whole frames at the measured rate. The 16/32-ms distractor cycle is exact only near 60 Hz, and the 175-ms SOA becomes 11 frames (183 ms) at 60 Hz; the realised SOA is recorded per trial
deviations.reason: alhazen times stimuli in display frames

deviations.here: Monkey parameter sets, and a human set: no stimulation (one control staircase), the target at a designated location, written instructions
deviations.reason: So the behavioural task can be piloted with volunteers; a human run says nothing about FEF stimulation

deviations.original: With the first monkey, % correct on stimulation vs control trials at arbitrary sub-threshold currents (17 sites, p. 1275)
deviations.here: Only the staircase procedure; the notebook reports % correct by condition from the staircase trials
deviations.reason: The threshold procedure is the paper's main measure; the fixed-level variant differs only in holding the dimming constant

tasks.title: Target dimming detection among flashing distractors
tasks.summary: Hold fixation; a target appears and distractors flash every 32 ms; press when the target dims, or hold off on a catch trial. On stimulation trials STIM_TRIGGER goes out one SOA before the dimming.

parameters.name: target_area_deg2
parameters.label: Target size
parameters.meaning: Area of the target square. ASSUMED within the paper's 0.25–1.25 deg².

parameters.name: distractor_area_deg2
parameters.label: Distractor size
parameters.meaning: Area of the distractor square. ASSUMED within the paper's 0.1–1 deg².

parameters.name: distractor_exclusion_dva
parameters.label: Distractor exclusion
parameters.meaning: Radius around the target where no distractor flashes. ASSUMED within the paper's 2–5°.

parameters.name: fix_size_dva
parameters.label: Fixation point size
parameters.meaning: Diameter of the fixation disc. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: fix_window_radius_dva
parameters.label: Fixation window
parameters.meaning: Radius of the window gaze must stay inside all trial. The paper's 3° window read as 3° across.

parameters.name: field.movement_field_dva
parameters.label: Movement field
parameters.meaning: Where suprathreshold stimulation sent the eyes this session, mapped by the lab. Example value.

parameters.name: field.target_field
parameters.label: Target field
parameters.meaning: inside: the target at the movement field; outside: rotated 90° about fixation, same eccentricity and hemifield.

parameters.name: dim_onset_min
parameters.label: Earliest dimming
parameters.meaning: Earliest dimming after target onset (paper: 500 ms).

parameters.name: dim_onset_max
parameters.label: Latest dimming
parameters.meaning: Latest dimming after target onset (paper: 1,300 ms).

parameters.name: response_window
parameters.label: Response window
parameters.meaning: Deadline for the response after the dimming. ASSUMED reading of the paper's 600–800 ms.

parameters.name: min_rt
parameters.label: Minimum reaction time
parameters.meaning: Presses sooner than this after the dimming count as early. ASSUMED.

parameters.name: catch_duration
parameters.label: Catch trial
parameters.meaning: How long the subject must hold off on a catch trial (paper: 2,100 ms).

parameters.name: stimulation.soa
parameters.label: Stimulation-onset asynchrony
parameters.meaning: STIM_TRIGGER precedes the dimming by this much (paper: 50–175 ms; 175 ms in Fig. 2c).

parameters.name: stimulation.enabled
parameters.label: Stimulation trials
parameters.meaning: Whether a stimulation staircase runs beside the control one (monkey sets only).

parameters.name: staircase.start_pct
parameters.label: Starting dimming
parameters.meaning: The staircases' starting level and ceiling. ASSUMED.

parameters.name: staircase.n_blocks
parameters.label: Blocks per staircase
parameters.meaning: Blocks each staircase runs. ASSUMED (the paper fitted 10–25).

outcomes.name: HIT
outcomes.meaning: A press within the response window after the dimming. Rewarded in monkey sessions.

outcomes.name: MISS
outcomes.meaning: No press within the response window after the dimming.

outcomes.name: EARLY_RESPONSE
outcomes.meaning: A press before the dimming, or sooner than the minimum reaction time after it.

outcomes.name: FALSE_ALARM
outcomes.meaning: A press on a catch trial.

outcomes.name: CORRECT_REJECTION
outcomes.meaning: No press for the whole catch trial. Rewarded in monkey sessions.

outcomes.name: FIX_BREAK
outcomes.meaning: Gaze left the fixation window; served again later in the same block.

outcomes.name: NO_FIXATION
outcomes.meaning: Fixation never acquired; served again later in the same block.

events.name: FIX_ACQUIRED
events.meaning: Gaze held inside the fixation window.

events.name: TARGET_ON
events.meaning: Target shown; the distractor cycle starts.

events.name: STIM_TRIGGER
events.meaning: Stimulation trials: one SOA before the (would-be) dimming. Map it to the stimulator's TTL line.

events.name: DIM_ON
events.meaning: First frame of the dimming; payload dim_pct (% Michelson) and dim_frames.

events.name: DIM_OFF
events.meaning: First frame back at full luminance.

events.name: RESPONSE
events.meaning: The subject's key; payload the outcome it produced.
